findings.quote: the Chair's recorded reading of 'comparable regimes' in section 3 as any law, regulation or standard that sets requirements for how records are kept, protected, retained, corrected or erased. On that reading, the medical-device rules EU MDR, 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485 and the rules for NMPA registration review are comparable regimes.
findings.problem: The author presents the Chair's personal reading as authoritative for the group's scope, expanding the charter's list of instruments without group consensus.
findings.fix: Replace 'the Chair's recorded reading' with 'a proposed interpretation' or similar, clarifying it is not an official group decision.

findings.quote: What these fifteen rows add is scored rows on the device side... These device instruments are not an aside: the Chair's recorded reading of section 3 names... and that reading is why they carry rows here.
findings.problem: The author justifies the inclusion of major new regulatory domains (medical devices) based solely on a single, non-consensus reading of the charter.
findings.fix: Acknowledge this is a proposal to expand scope, not an application of an agreed scope.

findings.quote: I did not obtain the ISO/IEC 42001:2023 text, which is why no clause number appears for it here; the annex says the same.
findings.problem: The author admits to not reading a key standard listed in the charter, yet includes a determination about it ('cannot be scored').
findings.fix: Either obtain the text or remove the instrument from the analysis with a note that it was omitted due to inaccessibility.

findings.quote: Treating that as a reason not to score it is an interpretive choice, and I record it as one rather than as a fact that settles the question
findings.problem: The author excludes NIST AI RMF (a charter-listed item) based on its voluntary nature, which is a substantive, debatable interpretation presented as a settled methodological choice.
findings.fix: Score it as 'not assessable' with the reason being the voluntary nature, or include it and note the challenge.

findings.quote: One row adds a sixth axis - attribution of the act to an authorised person - because Article 46(2) of China's GMP attaches the requirement to a person and not to a record; I flag it as an addition rather than pass it off as part of the Chair's reading.
findings.problem: The author modifies their own proposed unit (the five axes) mid-analysis to accommodate a finding from an instrument they introduced via the contested Chair's reading.
findings.fix: Stick to the originally proposed five axes for all instruments, or justify the new axis as a necessary expansion for all analyses.

findings.quote: China's device GMP - in force since 2026-11-01 - is the only instrument in the set whose requirements attach to the electronic record itself... in the archive record of this thread up to 2026-11-23 no one has mapped it.
findings.problem: Claims novelty ('no one has mapped it') for an analysis of an instrument the author themselves introduced to the discussion, which is self-serving.

findings.quote: The three section 3 items that are not scored are named here rather than left for a reader to discover, each with the reason
findings.problem: The phrasing 'rather than left for a reader to discover' frames the author as uniquely diligent, which is a subjective, self-serving framing.
findings.fix: Rephrase neutrally: 'The three section 3 items that are not scored, and the reason for each, are:'

findings.problem: Vague reference to an annex not included in the provided text. A reader cannot verify the claim.
findings.fix: Provide the specific statement from the annex or omit the phrase.

findings.quote: HIPAA's six-year rule (45 CFR 164.316(b)(2)(i)), by contrast, attaches, as I read it, to the documentation a covered entity must maintain
findings.problem: The phrase 'as I read it' highlights a personal, potentially contestable legal interpretation without supporting citation or argument.
findings.fix: Either state the interpretation confidently with supporting reasoning, or present it more tentatively as one possible view.

findings.quote: Those are Trial Use, so a precedent and not an authority - but they show the distinction is a field choice someone already made, not a new requirement invented here.
findings.problem: Dismisses the cited precedent ('not an authority') while simultaneously using it to argue the distinction is not novel, which is contradictory.
findings.fix: Either present it as a valid precedent or don't cite it. Remove 'not an authority'.
